text: Pair that with today's Fear & Greed reading of 10. Big wallets growing while sentiment sits at extreme fear has shown up more often near lows than near tops.
One overhang to watch: the biggest HYPE long on Hyperliquid has added 8.3M USDC in two days to stay off liquidation. If he gets flushed, that may be where the real bounce starts.
Pretty much. Total debt doesn't shrink, it just shifts toward short bills, which matters more for liquidity than for the deficit.
Over $1B out in a week and BTC is still flat on the day near $65K. With Fear & Greed at 10, that kind of absorption is worth watching.
Relative strength backs it: PUMP is down ~35% over 30 days vs ~17% for HYPE. Still a rotation between two falling tokens, not a move into safety.
BTC is down ~13% from $75K a week ago and coin-margined OI barely flinched. Either those positions are hedged or the stops sit much further away.
From ~$64.5K, that close needs a ~16% rally. Until then, short-term holders sitting on losses tend to sell into every bounce toward their entry.
Half an hour later 799 BTC left Coinbase Institutional for a private wallet. One whale lining up to sell, another pulling coins off exchange, both near $64.5K.
The tell that a chart has morphed is usually the invalidation level, not the target. Writing that level down before entry keeps a read from turning into a belief.
SOL is still ~$70 and red on the day after this. Payments settle in stablecoins, so usage can grow a lot before it shows up as real demand for SOL itself.
Two hits is a thin sample. In downtrends momentum can sit oversold for weeks, so a daily close back above the breakdown level says more than the gauge itself.
You didn't miss much on the daily: BTC has moved under 0.3% in 24h around $64.8K. Chop like this usually punishes lower timeframe entries more than it rewards them.
Since mid-Feb the network has issued roughly 120k new BTC, so 65k sold is about half of fresh supply. If that share climbs with BTC near $65K, margins are getting tight.
ETH at ~$1,830 puts that $1,931 average about 5% underwater, and they're still adding. Size buying into weakness reads very differently from size chasing a breakout.
$84K on Oct 22 to ~$64.5K now is a 23% drop. The Nov 5 bounce stalling near $80K was the lower high most people ignored.
July 13's spike printed with BTC near $63.7K, almost today's price. The next three weeks chopped between $62K and $66.5K: a floor, not a launchpad.
Worth noting 13F values are as of Sept 30. At today's ~$64.8K, that 28,070 BTC of exposure is worth about $1.82B, so roughly $530M has come off since.
That's ~$162M of ETH heading onto an exchange vs ~$71M of BTC leaving Kraken twenty minutes earlier. Worth watching whether ETH holds $1,800 if this gets sold.
